$comment: GENERATED by emit-sdk from synthetic_platform_manifest(). Declared schemas for the _platform.* collections.

_platform.actuator_log_level.description: Global log-level threshold for actuator.log (the TextFormatterSink). One record `{level}`; lines below the level are dropped. Default follows BRANCHKIT_LOG_LEVEL / `info`.

_platform.calibration.active.description: Platform-managed tag — set when a calibration trial is in progress, cleared on trial end. Plugins opt into defensive blocking during calibration by adding a `forbids_tag: _platform.calibration.active` policy on their own collections.

_platform.frozen_writers.description: Set of plugin:collection keys whose writes are frozen by the user.

_platform.input.description: Active input sessions, ONE RECORD PER INPUT PLUGIN — `active` is a fact about that plugin's world (true while it is capturing), `source` is the writing plugin id (also the record id), `directives` is a closed-vocabulary bag of platform-defined behavior flags. The platform reads the FOLD: the session is active if any writer's record says so, and a directive applies if any ACTIVE writer asserts it (`ActuatorState::input_state`). Records are writer-held, so a crashed input plugin's assertion drops instead of wedging every dispatch. This was a singleton — meaning the second input plugin ever written (foot pedal, eye tracker, MIDI…) would have silently clobbered voice's session and vice versa; per-writer records are what make input plugins a CATEGORY rather than a slot. The platform owns the schema; plugins write via `consumes.writes` (preferred) or `consumes.collections` (backwards compat) + the `anyone_who_declares` writers slot.

_platform.key_names.description: Key name → keycode for this platform. The NAME REGISTRY behind `input.press_key` with a `name`, and behind hotkey registration: whichever surface turns a spoken or written key name into an OS event resolves it here, so the four paths cannot disagree about which keys exist or how they are spelled. Platform-owned and platform-SEEDED (see `collection_data` below): named keys work on a bare install with no plugins, which is the point — this used to be a plugin-introduced collection called `keycodes`, and the platform's ability to press `return` was hostage to the keyboard plugin being installed. That made key naming a SLOT; per the same reasoning as `_platform.input`, it should be a category. `writers: anyone_who_declares` is what makes it one: a remapper, an alternative-layout plugin, or hardware support can extend or correct the baseline, and users edit it like any other collection. `code` is authoritative where the OS injects by numeric keycode (macOS virtual keycodes). Off macOS the actuator resolves names through enigo's and global_hotkey's own vocabularies, and `code` carries that platform's native value for reference; see docs/design/DESIGN_SHAPED_CONSUMPTION.md for why those two encodings are not interchangeable.

_platform.log_retention.description: Per-sink archive retention overrides for the dated-gzip archiving sinks (audit_log, show_all, dev_mutation_stream, verbose). One record per overridden sink `{sink, days}`; a sink with no record keeps its env-seeded default (90/30/30/7). Set from the Debug tab; applied live.

_platform.model_download.description: In-flight model download progress from the platform shell (which runs the downloader). Single record at id='_platform'.

_platform.never_standalone_penalty.description: Lever E never-standalone decoding penalty (command recognition accuracy). One record `{penalty}`; 0/absent = off. Applied to words that can never start a command (numbers, app names, ...) so codewords win the decode.

_platform.pipelines.description: Pipeline records — typed streaming compositions of stages. Each record describes how signals flow through stage implementations contributed by plugins until a decision-maker emits an action call. The platform owns the schema; plugins contribute records via `consumes.collections`.

_platform.plugin_log_thresholds.description: Per-plugin log-level threshold for the plugin.debug RPC. Lines below the threshold are dropped at the handler. Default is `info`.

_platform.plugins.data_disposition.description: Uninstall markers: what collections a removed plugin owned and when it was removed, read by the boot-time orphan sweep.

_platform.plugins.disabled.description: Set of plugin IDs the user has explicitly disabled.

_platform.plugins.interaction_grants.description: Per-plugin interaction grants (dispatch, event subscription, collection read).

_platform.plugins.privilege_grants.description: Privileges the user has approved per plugin.

_platform.plugins.trusted_authors.description: Authors the user has bulk-trusted for cross-plugin interaction.

_platform.plugins.uninstalled.description: Set of bundled plugin IDs the user has explicitly uninstalled.

_platform.stage_log_thresholds.description: Per-stage log-level threshold for pipeline-stage diagnostics. Structured lines below the threshold are dropped before emission. Default is `info`.

_platform.user_commands.description: User-created voice commands (CRUD via Settings UI).
